title: Stochastic Convex Optimization for Day-Ahead Shared Battery Storage Scheduling in Solar Energy Communities
abstract: Energy communities represent a transformative paradigm for decentralized renewable energy integration, enabling collective investment in photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems (BESS) to achieve economic and environmental benefits. However, the optimal operation of these communities faces significant challenges due to inherent uncertainties in solar generation, load consumption, and electricity prices. This paper presents a stochastic optimization framework for day-ahead scheduling of shared battery energy storage in solar-powered energy communities under multiple uncertainty sources. The problem is formulated as a stochastic mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) model that minimizes the expected daily operational cost, including energy procurement from the grid, PV operation and maintenance (O&M), battery operation costs, and degradation-induced expenses. A battery degradation model based on equivalent full-cycle counting captures the economic impact of cycling under uncertain conditions. The proposed approach employs a scenario-based Monte Carlo method to represent uncertainties and reformulates the MINLP as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) through exact linearization of the absolute-value terms in the degradation cost, enabling efficient solution with commercial solvers. The framework is applied to an aggregated energy community whose installed PV capacity (6.888 MW) and shared BESS capacity (2.1667 MWh) are defined from the resource distribution of a modified IEEE 33-bus network; the aggregation focuses on the energy-time dimension of the scheduling problem, and network voltages, branch flows and locational losses are not represented. The value of the stochastic solution (VSS) is 2319.74 USD/day, showing that the stochastic schedule is substantially cheaper than the deterministic schedule when evaluated on the same uncertain scenario set. A robustness study over 30 random seeds gives an expected cost of 11,825.77 ± 295.83 USD/day. Relative to the no-storage baseline, the shared BESS reduces the expected daily cost by about 1.2%, and the terminal-SoC relaxation reduces the cost by a further 194.61 USD/day. The MILP formulation and its continuous relaxation produce the same optimum, confirming that the binary variables are not needed at the optimum.
title_zh: Stochastic Convex Optimization for Day-Ahead Shared Battery Storage Scheduling in Solar Energy Communities

title: Comparative Sensitivity Analysis of Grid‐Scale Battery Storage Technologies: Feasibility Investigation for Solar Integration in India
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a comprehensive techno‐economic and environmental sensitivity analysis of integrating grid‐scale solar photovoltaic systems with multiple energy storage technologies to fulfill state‐level electricity demand in Jharkhand, India—a resource‐rich and coal‐dependent state facing persistent grid reliability challenges. Addressing a critical research gap in sector‐specific, multi‐chemistry storage optimization under dynamic tariff regimes, the study models and compares four storage technologies—lithium ferro phosphate batteries (LFP), sodium‐sulfur batteries (NaS), vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFB), and pumped hydropower storage (PH), each tailored for six‐hour charge retention. The open‐source Solar Alone Multi‐objective Advisor (SAMA) tool, used to model PV‐battery hybrids, has been used with particle swarm optimization. One hundred and twenty‐eight system configurations were simulated across fixed and time‐of‐use tariffs, with and without net metering, under varying inflation (5%–12.5%) and grid price escalation rates (−2.5% to +5%). The analysis rigorously assesses each configuration's payback period, internal rate of return (IRR), return on investment (RoI), levelized cost of energy (LCOE), emissions, and system sizing metrics. The results show that LFP batteries consistently deliver the shortest payback periods (8–13 years), the highest RoI (43%–340%), and the most stable IRR (9%–13%) under all market scenarios, marking them as the most bankable near‐term solution for daily cycling. Pumped hydropower provides moderate payback periods (10–18 years) and achieves highly competitive LCOE values (USD 0.03–0.04 per kWh with net metering), making it ideal for large‐scale, long‐duration storage where suitable sites exist. Sodium‐sulfur batteries reach RoI up to 288% in high‐inflation scenarios but display greater volatility, while vanadium redox flow batteries, with payback periods of 11–22 years and no mid‐life replacements, offer unique advantages for deep‐cycling, stationary industrial applications. Net metering emerges as a dominant policy lever, reducing LCOE from USD 0.06–0.16 per kWh (no export) to USD 0.03–0.04 per kWh (with export) and cutting lifecycle emissions from 0.45 to 0.17 kg/kWh, while enabling a surge in optimal installed PV capacity from 3–5 GW to over 16 GW. The findings accentuate that while LFP offers superior financial performance and rapid capital recovery, sector‐specific technology mapping is essential to maximize grid resilience and renewable integration by deploying NaS and PH for medium and bulk storage, and VRFB for industrial deep cycling. Ultimately, the study provides a replicable, data‐driven framework for selecting and optimizing storage technologies under evolving market structures, supporting Jharkhand's and similar regions' transition from coal reliance to a resilient, renewable‐powered future.

title: Frequency-decoupled dynamic graph learning with degradation prior for robust state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries
abstract: State-of-health (SOH) estimation of lithium-ion batteries is critical for reliable battery management in energy storage systems, where SOH must be inferred from noisy multi-frequency health indicators under varying operating conditions. Existing methods often fail to decouple multi-frequency degradation information, capture dynamic couplings among health indicators, and preserve consistency with degradation mechanisms, which limits their robustness across temperatures and chemistries. To address these issues, this study proposes a degradation-prior-enhanced frequency-decoupled dynamic graph learning framework for robust SOH estimation. STL decomposition is first employed to separate low-frequency degradation trends from high-frequency fluctuations, each handled by a dedicated temporal branch. A degradation-guided dynamic graph module is then developed, integrating health-indicator coupling priors and degradation-direction consistency priors to suppress spurious correlations. Finally, degradation-guided loss terms are embedded to encourage SOH trajectories consistent with battery aging behavior. Experiments on three public datasets (NASA, CALCE, and Zhu et al. dataset) show that the proposed method achieves an average mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.798%, outperforming mainstream baselines. In the cross-temperature transfer experiments, compared with the best-performing baseline GRU, the proposed method reduces the average root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) by 57.41% and 60.03%, respectively, indicating greater robustness and more reliable support for battery health management in practical battery monitoring.
title_zh: Frequency-decoupled dynamic graph learning with degradation prior for robust state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries

title: Physics-informed learning of health-aware equivalent circuit parameter evolution for lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries exhibit nonlinear degradation under complex operating conditions and long-term cycling. Existing studies mainly focus on state-of-health (SOH) estimation, while continuous SOC–SOH-dependent ECM parameter representation and validation of neural-network-inverted parameters remain limited. This study proposes an ECM-PINN framework that integrates a neural network with a differentiable first-order RC model for joint SOH estimation, ECM parameter inversion, and voltage reconstruction. An SOH-guided consistency regularization is introduced to regulate excessive cross-cell parameter dispersion. The framework is evaluated on the Samsung 50E and HUST datasets. On unseen Samsung 50E cells, the Pearson correlation coefficients between the inverted and conventionally identified R 0 , R 1 , and C 1 are 0.996, 0.998, and 0.992, respectively. On the HUST dataset, the SOH estimation MAE and RMSE are 0.53% and 0.74%, while the voltage reconstruction MAE and RMSE are 20.50 mV and 26.00 mV. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can perform SOC–SOH-dependent ECM parameter inversion under both standardized HPPC and non-standard dynamic operating conditions, while maintaining stable SOH estimation and voltage reconstruction performance.
title_zh: Physics-informed learning of health-aware equivalent circuit parameter evolution for lithium-ion batteries
